note: Requirements reference taxonomy topics by stableKey. Only topics that exist in the published taxonomy are seeded; the rest are reported and skipped, so the catalogue grows as content does rather than referencing topics that are not there.

roles.title: Security Operations Analyst
roles.summary: Monitors security alerts, investigates suspicious activity and escalates genuine incidents. Entry routes usually expect clear written handover and calm escalation under time pressure.

requirements.rationale: Incident handover and escalation notes are read by people acting on them under pressure.
Security interviews probe reasoning aloud through scenario questions.

roles.title: Software Engineer
roles.summary: Builds and maintains software with a team. Entry routes weigh problem solving alongside the ability to explain a decision to people who did not write the code.

requirements.rationale: Code review and design discussion are written and spoken work.
Technical interviews are largely explaining your approach while you work.

roles.title: Data Analyst
roles.summary: Turns data into answers people can act on. The analysis matters less than whether the conclusion is understood and trusted by whoever has to decide.

requirements.rationale: An analysis nobody understands changes no decision.
Case-style interviews ask you to reason through an ambiguous question aloud.

roles.title: Business Analyst
roles.summary: Works between business teams and delivery teams, turning what people ask for into something that can be built and checked.

requirements.rationale: The role is almost entirely eliciting, writing down and confirming what was meant.
Interviews test whether you can structure an unclear problem in conversation.

roles.title: Customer Success Associate
roles.summary: Helps customers get value from a product and keeps a relationship healthy, including when something has gone wrong.

requirements.rationale: Difficult conversations handled well are the substance of the role.
Interviews lean on worked examples from your own experience.
